title: Integrated Management System — Apex Manual

scope_cards.label: Purpose
scope_cards.text: This Integrated Management System (IMS) Manual defines the Quality, Environmental, and Occupational Health & Safety Management Systems of Pack Masters. It demonstrates compliance with ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015, and ISO 45001:2018 requirements, and provides a framework for continual improvement of processes and customer satisfaction.

scope_cards.label: Scope
scope_cards.text: Contract Packaging Services including Repacking of Industrial Chemicals, Adhesives, Lubricant Oils, Greases, Fuel Additives, Agro Chemicals & Solvents. Applicable to all departments, processes, and personnel at the Pack Masters facility in India.

scope_cards.label: Responsible
scope_cards.text: Balkrishna Mishra (CEO / Managing Director) — overall accountability. Tarun Mishra (General Manager – Operations / ISO Document Approval Authority) — implementation and oversight. Ms. Khushi Paswan (Quality Management Representative) — maintenance and continual improvement of the IMS.

policy_statement: Pack Masters is committed to providing high-quality contract packaging services while safeguarding the environment and ensuring the health & safety of all workers. Our Integrated Management System (IMS) is designed to meet the requirements of ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015, and ISO 45001:2018. We pledge to continually improve our processes, prevent pollution, eliminate hazards and reduce OH&S risks, comply with applicable legal and regulatory requirements, and meet the needs and expectations of our interested parties.

sub_sections.title: Understanding the Organization & its Context
sub_sections.content: The Integrated Management System at Packmasters is realized through adoption of ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015, ISO 45001:2018, ISO 50001:2018, and ISO 31000:2018. Packmasters determines external and internal issues relevant to its purpose and strategic direction through SWOT analysis, with continuous monitoring and review by Top Management.

sub_sections.title: Understanding the Needs & Expectations of Interested Parties
Determining the Scope of the IMS
sub_sections.content: The scope of the Integrated Management System of Packmasters encompasses all quality, environmental, occupational health & safety, energy management, and risk management activities conducted at the Rabale facility, covering all stages from receipt of raw materials through production, quality control, and dispatch of finished packaged goods.

sub_sections.title: IMS & its Processes
sub_sections.content: Packmasters has established, documented, implemented, maintained, and continually improves its IMS in accordance with all five referenced standards. Processes are identified in Annexure I and their interactions depicted in Annexure IV. The EnMS processes (energy review, energy planning, energy monitoring) and the Risk Management processes (risk identification, RPN scoring, risk register maintenance) are integrated into the existing process map as support processes.

sub_sections.title: Leadership & Commitment
sub_sections.content:
Top Management of Packmasters demonstrates commitment to the IMS (including EnMS and Risk Management) by:
Communicating the importance of meeting customer, statutory, regulatory, and energy compliance requirements.
Establishing and communicating IMS Policy including Quality, Environment, OH&S, and Energy policies.
Appointing the Management Coordinator and allocating responsibilities across all five system dimensions.
Ensuring integration of QMS, EMS, OHSMS, EnMS, and Risk Management into business processes.
Promoting risk-based thinking, process approach, and energy performance improvement culture.
Conducting Management Review Meetings at prescribed intervals with agenda covering all systems.
Ensuring availability of resources — human, financial, technological — for the complete IMS.
Championing energy conservation goals and risk mitigation across all functions.

sub_sections.title: Customer Focus
sub_sections.content: Management ensures customer and applicable statutory requirements are determined and consistently met. Risks and opportunities affecting service conformity and customer satisfaction are addressed through the Risk Register (ML-30). Customer feedback is collected through visits, interface meetings, and satisfaction surveys on a half-yearly basis.

sub_sections.title: IMS Policy
sub_sections.content:
Pack Masters maintains an integrated policy covering Quality, Environment, OH&S, and Energy commitments. The policy is approved by the Proprietor, documented in English and Hindi, communicated at all levels, displayed at strategic locations, and reviewed at every MRM for continuing suitability. The Quality Policy is documented as a standalone controlled document (PM-QP-001) and the Environmental Policy as PM-EP-001. Both are displayed at the factory premises and available to relevant interested parties.
The Energy Policy specifically commits to:
Achieving energy performance improvement through the systematic EnMS process.
Ensuring availability of information and resources to achieve energy objectives and targets.
Complying with applicable energy-related legal requirements.
Supporting procurement of energy-efficient products and services.

sub_sections.title: Organizational Roles, Responsibilities & Authorities
sub_sections.content: Top Management has defined roles and responsibilities communicated through the organizational chart (Annexure II) and Responsibility Matrix (Annexure III). Additional responsibilities for EnMS and Risk Management are:

sub_sections.title: Actions to Address Risks & Opportunities (ISO 31000:2018)
sub_sections.content: Packmasters has established a formal Risk Management framework in accordance with ISO 31000:2018, operationalized through Risk Analysis Procedure Pr-02 and Risk Register ML-30. This framework addresses risks and opportunities across all IMS processes.

sub_sections.title: Risk Identification Methodology
sub_sections.content:
Risks and opportunities are identified by respective Heads of Departments (HODs) for each process by collecting information from:
Previous customer complaints and non-conformances
Lessons learnt from past incidents and near-misses
Legal and regulatory requirements
Customer-specific requirements (CSR)
Process monitoring data and historical performance
SWOT analysis outputs (Cl. 4.1)
Energy performance deviations (for EnMS-related risks)

sub_sections.title: RPN Scoring & Categorization (Ref: Pr-02)
sub_sections.content: Risk Priority Number (RPN) = Severity × Occurrence × Detection

sub_sections.title: Risk Register Summary (Ref: ML-30) — Top Significant Risks
sub_sections.content: The following processes have been identified with significant risks (RPN > 30) from the Risk Register ML-30. Full details are provided in Annexure VII.

sub_sections.title: Quality / Environmental / OH&S Objectives & Planning
sub_sections.content:
Objectives are established annually by Top Management and MC, consistent with IMS policy, and reviewed at every MRM. Objectives are measurable, practical, and linked to KPIs.
Quality Objectives: Customer satisfaction, on-time delivery, reduction in NCRs, new product development.
Environmental Objectives: Reduction of waste, reduction of energy consumption (linked to EnMS), compliance with environmental regulations.
OH&S Objectives: Zero lost-time incidents, 100% PPE compliance, completion of safety training programs.
Energy Objectives: Reduce energy consumption per unit by defined targets; complete energy audit annually.

sub_sections.title: Planning of Changes
sub_sections.content: Changes to the IMS are planned considering: purpose and potential consequences, integrity of the management system, resource availability, and reallocation of responsibilities. Changes to EnMS processes (e.g., modification of SEUs) or Risk Register updates (RPN re-assessment) are managed through the same change control mechanism.

sub_sections.title: OH&S Planning — Hazard Identification & Risk Assessment (HIRA)
sub_sections.content: HIRA is conducted for all key operational processes. Controls are identified and implemented in a planned manner, documented in DP 09. The HIRA process is aligned with the ISO 31000:2018 risk framework, using consistent terminology for hazard identification, risk evaluation, and control hierarchy.

sub_sections.title: Energy Management Planning (ISO 50001:2018)
sub_sections.content: Packmasters has established an Energy Management System in accordance with ISO 50001:2018 to systematically improve energy performance across all production and support processes.

sub_sections.title: Energy Policy
sub_sections.content:
The Energy Policy of Packmasters commits to:
Continual improvement of energy performance, energy efficiency, and reduction of energy intensity.
Ensuring availability of information and resources to achieve energy objectives and targets.
Compliance with all applicable energy-related legal and regulatory requirements.
Supporting procurement of energy-efficient products, equipment, and services.
Design of facilities and processes with energy performance improvement in mind.
The Energy Policy is approved by the Proprietor, communicated to all personnel, and reviewed annually at MRM.

sub_sections.title: Energy Review & Baseline (EnB)
sub_sections.content:
An Energy Review is conducted annually (DP 18) to:
Analyze energy sources, past and present energy consumption data.
Identify Significant Energy Uses (SEUs) — processes/equipment with highest energy consumption.
Identify variables affecting energy consumption (production volume, ambient temperature, shift patterns).
Estimate future energy use and consumption trends.
The Energy Baseline (EnB) is established using 12 months of historical data as the reference period and is updated when significant changes in operations, facilities, or equipment occur.

sub_sections.title: Resources
sub_sections.content: Packmasters provides resources for establishment, implementation, maintenance, and continual improvement of the IMS including QMS, EMS, OHSMS, EnMS, and Risk Management. Additional resources for EnMS include energy metering equipment, sub-meters, and energy monitoring software/log sheets. Resources for Risk Management include ML-30 documentation, RPN tracking tools, and training on Pr-02.

sub_sections.title: Competence
sub_sections.content: Personnel assigned IMS responsibilities are competent based on education, training, skills, and experience. Competency requirements now include: understanding of energy performance monitoring and EnPI reporting; ability to conduct or participate in risk assessment using the RPN methodology (Pr-02); and awareness of the Risk Register (ML-30) relevant to their function.

sub_sections.title: Awareness
sub_sections.content: All employees are made aware of the IMS policy including the Energy Policy; their contribution to energy performance improvement; the risks associated with their work activities and the RPN-based framework; consequences of departure from IMS requirements; and their role in emergency preparedness.

sub_sections.title: Communication
sub_sections.content: Internal communication on EnMS includes monthly EnPI reports shared at MRM, energy conservation notices displayed at SEU locations, and training programs. External communication on EnMS includes regulatory submissions to BEE (if applicable) and energy audit reports. Risk-related communication includes RPN trend reports at MRM and updated Risk Register (ML-30) distribution to all HODs.

sub_sections.title: Documented Information
sub_sections.content: The IMS documentation structure follows a four-level hierarchy:

sub_sections.title: Operational Planning & Control
sub_sections.content: Packmasters plans, implements, and controls all processes needed for product/service provision. Operational controls are established for significant environmental aspects, OH&S risks, and Significant Energy Uses (SEUs). Risk controls identified in ML-30 for RPN > 30 are embedded as operational controls within relevant DPMs.

sub_sections.title: Requirements of Products & Services
sub_sections.content: Customer communication, requirement determination, and review processes are conducted as per established procedures. Emergency Preparedness and Response procedures cover potential environmental and OH&S emergencies and are reviewed at least annually.

sub_sections.title: Production & Service Provision
sub_sections.content:
Production is executed under controlled conditions per production plans, process sheets, and work instructions. Identification and traceability are maintained for finished products. Post-delivery activities and control of changes are managed per documented procedures.
Production Standard Operating Procedures (PM/SOP/PD-01 to PM/SOP/PD-06) cover Downfilling, Labelling, Lid Press, Acetone Primer Downfilling, Acetone Storage & Handling, and Stirrer operations. These SOPs define process parameters, quality checkpoints, PPE requirements (where applicable), and responsible personnel for each production step.

sub_sections.title: Release of Products & Services
sub_sections.content: Products are released only upon satisfactory completion of all planned inspection and test arrangements. Evidence of conformity is retained as documented information.

sub_sections.title: Control of Non-Conforming Products
sub_sections.content: Non-conforming products are identified, segregated, and dispositioned per documented procedures. Corrective actions are initiated and tracked. Non-conformances with RPN implications are escalated through the Risk Register (ML-30) update process.

sub_sections.title: Monitoring, Measurement, Analysis & Evaluation
sub_sections.content: Packmasters monitors and measures performance across all IMS dimensions. The Management Review agenda includes EnPI performance vs targets, RPN trend analysis from ML-30, and energy audit findings. Customer satisfaction is measured half-yearly. Compliance evaluations cover legal, regulatory, and energy-related requirements.

sub_sections.title: Internal Audit
sub_sections.content: Internal Audits are conducted at least twice per year covering all departments and all five IMS standards. The audit programme (planned by MC) now includes: QMS audit per ISO 9001:2015; EMS audit per ISO 14001:2015; OHSMS audit per ISO 45001:2018; EnMS audit per ISO 50001:2018 (DP 19); and Risk Management process audit verifying ML-30 currency and RPN review frequency. Auditors must be trained and independent of the area being audited. The Internal Audit Checklist (PM-IAC-001) provides a comprehensive clause-by-clause checklist covering ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 14001:2015 requirements (Clauses 4–10) with evidence references mapped to this Apex Manual, procedures, and registers.

sub_sections.title: Management Review
sub_sections.content:
MRM inputs include all standard agenda items plus: EnPI performance vs baseline and targets; status of energy objectives and action plans; significant energy uses and any changes; results of energy audits (DP 19); RPN trends and status of significant risk mitigation actions; and changes in legal requirements affecting energy or risk.
MRM outputs include decisions on: resource allocation for energy improvements; updates to EnPIs, EnB, and energy objectives; updates to Risk Register (ML-30); and approval of new documented procedures arising from risk assessment.

sub_sections.title: General
sub_sections.content: Packmasters continually improves the effectiveness of the IMS through: audit results, analysis of data, corrective actions, MRM outputs, and management of risks and opportunities. Energy performance improvement is a specific continual improvement dimension tracked through EnPI trends.

sub_sections.title: Non-Conformity & Corrective Action
sub_sections.content: All non-conformances — including energy performance deviations and risk events — are addressed through corrective action (DP 04). When a risk event occurs that was not captured in ML-30, the Risk Register is updated with the new risk, severity, occurrence, and detection scores. If RPN > 30, a documented procedure or work instruction is established within the defined timeframe.

sub_sections.title: Continual Improvement
sub_sections.content:
Continual improvement is pursued across all five IMS dimensions — QMS, EMS, OHSMS, EnMS, and Risk Management — through use of IMS Policy, objectives, audit results, data analysis, corrective actions, management review, and energy performance trends. Breakthrough improvements and innovation are encouraged, particularly in energy conservation and risk elimination.
ANNEXURE I — List of Procedures Referenced for Processes

ANNEXURE III — Roles, Responsibilities & Authorities
Detailed roles and responsibilities are defined in the Integrated Procedure Manual. Key responsibilities for EnMS and Risk Management are described in Sections 5.4 and 6.1 of this manual.
ANNEXURE IV — Sequence & Interaction of Processes
The process map and interactions follow the PDCA cycle: Plan (Context, Leadership, Planning) → Do (Support, Operations) → Check (Performance Evaluation) → Act (Improvement). EnMS processes (Energy Review, EnPI monitoring, Energy Audit) and Risk processes (Risk Register maintenance, RPN review) are integrated as support and check-phase activities.

doc_numbering.description: All IMS documents follow a structured coding convention to ensure traceability and easy identification.
doc_numbering.versioning: Documents use major.minor versioning (e.g., v3.1). Major versions indicate significant revisions; minor versions indicate editorial changes.

distribution_control.description: This manual is a controlled document. Distribution, access, and obsolescence are managed as follows:

items.title: Controlled Copies
items.text: Electronic controlled copies are maintained on the company digital QMS platform. Hard copies are uncontrolled unless stamped CONTROLLED COPY with a distribution number.

items.title: Access
items.text: All employees can access the current version via the QMS platform. External parties (auditors, customers) may access read-only versions upon approval by the QMR.

items.title: Obsolete Versions
items.text: Superseded versions are archived in the QMS platform with OBSOLETE watermark. Physical copies are retrieved and destroyed by the Document Controller.

items.title: Revision Authority
items.text: Only the ISO Document Approval Authority (Tarun Mishra) can approve revisions. The Document Controller (Khushi Paswan) manages distribution.

change_management.description: Changes to IMS documents follow a structured amendment process to maintain system integrity:

steps.title: Change Request
steps.text: Any employee can initiate a change request using the Change Request Form (PM/FRM/CHG-01), specifying the reason and proposed change.

steps.title: Impact Assessment
steps.text: The QMR evaluates the impact on other documents, processes, and standards compliance using the Change Impact Assessment Form (PM/FRM/CHG-02).

steps.title: Review & Approval
steps.text: Changes are reviewed by relevant process owners and approved by the ISO Document Approval Authority.

steps.title: Implementation
steps.text: The Document Controller updates the document, increments the version, updates the revision history, and distributes the new version.

steps.title: Communication
steps.text: Affected personnel are notified of changes through departmental briefings, training sessions, or QMS platform notifications.

steps.title: Tracking
steps.text: All changes are logged in the Change Register (PM/REG/CHG-01) with traceability to the original request.

Coordinating internal audits and management review meetings

process_approach.description: Pack Masters adopts the Process Approach as required by ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015, and ISO 45001:2018. All activities are managed as interrelated processes within the PDCA (Plan-Do-Check-Act) cycle to achieve intended outcomes effectively.

pdca.description: Establish objectives, identify risks & opportunities, determine resources, and plan processes to deliver results aligned with customer requirements, environmental obligations, and OH&S commitments.
Implement the planned processes. Execute operations according to SOPs, work instructions, and operational controls. Provide training and ensure competence.
Monitor, measure, and evaluate process performance against objectives and KPIs. Conduct internal audits, management reviews, and compliance evaluations.
Take corrective actions on nonconformities, implement improvements, update risk assessments, and drive continual improvement of IMS effectiveness.
